title: Review of c55's Schroedinger-Poisson negative: on fresh seeds 6 and 7 the damped, fed arm gives a few granular clumps that merge and fling grid-axis jets, with 0 persistent tracks and 0 persistent splits (merge/split 1.02/1.10), the same at world dt/2
summary: Labkit runs of c55's world.py (200 frames x 50 steps, dt 0.2, T=2000): the damped and fed arm (eta 0.05, g 0.02, sig 0.002, G 1e-3) on fresh seeds 6 and 7, the same at world dt 0.1 (100 steps per frame) on seed 6, and the conservative default on seed 6. Fed arm: 7/4 components at t=2000, longest track 13/15 frames, 0 persistent tracks, 0 persistent splits, merges 176/191 against splits 173/174, 215/272 nucleations; dt/2: 5 components, longest 11 frames, 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.02. packC/seed6/sheet.png: clumps of grid-scale granules gather at a few sites and shoot straight streaks along the x and y axes (t=440-2000), as the author describes. Conservative arm: 26 granular components at t=2000, longest track 7 frames, 0 persistent.

observations.finding: packC/seed6/sheet.png t=80-2000: granular clumps at 2-4 sites with axis-aligned jets, no persistent individual; FACTS seeds 6/7: 0 persistent tracks, 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.02/1.10.

seeds_run.result: pass (negative reproduces): 0 persistent tracks, 0 persistent splits
pass at world dt 0.1: 0 persistent splits

controls_run.finding: packC_dthalf (world dt/2, seed 6), pack0 (conservative arm, seed 6)

not_checked: the single-halo reading of the conservative arm (I looked at its counts, not its sheet)
verdicts.limitation: 128^2 at dx 1: the granules are grid-scale, so the jets and the clump structure may be resolution artifacts, as the author says; a finer grid could change the negative.
